brain kind of like, wow, when I discovered that. I wonder what the challenge and tension is there with trying to translate a deep, potentially profound opportunity for access for incarcerated people to learning of cultural history that they may not have

had access to previously. And these perhaps simplistic other measuring tools like re-offending rates. Mm. You know what I mean? Like-... are we trying to fit a round peg into a square hole or vice versa with how the value of fulfilling that treaty obligation, in this instance, to recognize the disproportionate number of Māori in corrections and the acknowledgement that the Treaty of Waitangi tribunal made was that Corrections was failing in its obligations to account for that.

That then that has to be justified by some sort of other measure of success and the value of having high capability there. I do agree with you. Sometimes things just add inherent value to them. I think if we lift this up a little bit, just on this measuring bit, because we have a lot of discussions about the fact that, number one, multiple governments, not just the government of the day, multiple governments with Māori, for you to attain more resources- Mm... you actually must have to prove that your systems work.

So measurability is really important. And I think, personally, I believe there's a bigger emphasis on Māori outcomes in achieving that than in a lot of other places in our government. But that aside, that's number one. But if we lift this up, I think we've got three very important entities that which you have identified in the report, and that's the Public Service Commission, Treasury, and TPK.

At that level there, I see that number one, the Public Service Commission, they set the incentive or not of the CEO- Yeah... of each organization as to how they perform. If you do not have a KPI- Mm... on their books as to deliver Māori outcomes. Dare I say it, you won't have the emphasis required to get the change. That's number one.

Number two, Treasury. Measuring. Mm. Measuring dollar spends to Steve's point about how do we actually truly work out the outcomes are being attained- Mm... for the investment made of taxpayer dollar to help us get even more investment where it works well and all that sort of stuff.

And number three, TPK.
